data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 conjectures that the four guarantees follow from the labeling operator being monotone AND inflationary on the complete lattice of labelings, and that reinstatement and root validity are theorems of monotonicity. This is false because monotonicity and inflationarity do not entail committed-root validity. Take the lattice {IN, OUT, UNDEC} and the operator F(L)(x) = IN for every node x, regardless of the graph. F is trivially monotone and inflationary (with IN at the top of the lattice), and its unique fixpoint is the all-IN labeling. But if a committed root has an undefeated attacker, that root cannot be validly accepted, so all-IN violates committed-root validity. Thus a monotone, inflationary operator is not sufficient for the guarantees; reinstatement and root validity are not theorems of monotonicity alone.
